- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment to dampen forecast volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is near historical mean, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day price and sentiment to anchor forecast.
